title: bias-variance tradeoff
body: Hello Code2Vec Team You mentioned in your paper Code2Vec that there are two main challenges in your work 1 how you can decompose a program into smaller building blocks such that 1 large enough to be meaningful and 2 small enough to repeat across programs You then defined the previous 2 points as a bias variance tradeoff Can you please explain this idea more

comments.body: Hi Avv22 Thank you for your interest in our work and thank you for reading the paper carefully This is a great question The bias variance trade off is a general concept in machine learning that expresses the main problem in designing features or representations in machine learning models Too specific features may describe the training data very well but can cause overfitting too general simple features may occur across many examples but can be insufficiently expressive For more information see the Wikipedia article for example https en m wikipedia org wiki Bias E2 80 93variance tradeoff Best Uri

title: How is AST path converted to vector?
body: Came here from https youtu be EJ8okcxL2Iw t 426 The talk says there are token vectors and path vectors I know what an AST is but I am not that proficient in AI to answer what is the token vector Is it a list of all tokens encountered Or a list of all possible combinations of token pair It also not clear what a path vector is If I understand it right then vector should contains numbers not symbols from AST path So how does AST path is converted to path vector Does the path vector include leaves which are tokens symbols

comments.body: Hi abitrolly Thank you for your interest in our work Every unique token and unique path in the training data is allocated with a randomly initialized vector and we remember the mapping between every token path into its ID an integer and between every ID to the allocated vector Initially these vectors are meaningless since they are random but then these vectors are trained as part of the neural network This is a common practice in neural networks also known as word embeddings I recommend also reading the paper https urialon cswp cs technion ac il wp content uploads sites 83 2018 12 code2vec popl19 pdf Best Uri

Hi Uri Thanks for the fast reply I am not really familiar with embeddings so while reading the paper https urialon cswp cs technion ac il wp content uploads sites 83 2018 12 code2vec popl19 pdf right now the reference to continuous vectors for representing snippets of code doesn t make it more clear Need some low level example like requested in 102 to get a picture of what this code embedding is composed of And a 3D movie of the process D It is also interesting to see how a parallel vocabulary of vectors of the labels looks like and how does his vector arithmetic with words actually works That s already a lot of questions and I haven t even started with chapter 1 1 Applications D So I better skip directly to 2 1 Motivating Example which contains the following explanation Path extraction First each query method in the training corpus is parsed to construct an AST Then the AST is traversed and syntactic paths between AST leaves are extracted Each path is represented as a sequence of AST nodes linked by up and down arrows which symbolize the up or down link between adjacent nodes in the tree The path composition is kept with the values of the AST leaves it is connecting as a tuple we refer to as a path context Right now I understand the process as following mermaid graph LR java AST L leaves and paths E vector AKA code embedding Chapter 3 gives some hard mathematical abstractions Thankfully I played a bit with https docs python org 3 library ast html to modify Python sources with Python so I won t break my head on formal AST definition and can skip over D At the end there is a useful example of leaves and paths This expression x 7 Is transformed into leaves x and 7 and the path NameExpr AssignExpr IntegerLiteralExpr between them x NameExpr AssignExpr IntegerLiteralExpr 7 So this thing is called Path Context The paper then gives some limitations To limit the size of the training data and reduce sparsity we limit the paths by maximum length and limit the maximum width the maximal difference in child index between two child nodes of the same intermediate node These values are determined empirically as hyperparameters of our model This needs example Like the length of AST is actually depth of nesting instructions and the width is the difference between line number in the same method without nesting But I may be wrong here values are determined empirically as hyperparameters of our model breaks my mind Is it about that parameters are calculated during dataset preprocessing to keep dataset small Finally chapter 4 MODEL explains high level view and jumps directly to a Bag of Path Contexts while I am still puzzled how a single Path Context consisting of mathematical symbols is represented in data on low level For example this one x NameExpr AssignExpr IntegerLiteralExpr 7 How it looks in Python code And then if I understand it right everything in this tuple needs to be a digit because Python do not understand math symbols like these and because to train model there should be arithmetic operations there And that tuple with digits is what I meant by vector while writing the title for this issue There are a lot questions about the bag about the size of every to every dict of leaves what is node and itself in pairs that contain a node and itself but that falls out of scope for this question Originally I was going about to ask if the vector is this csv id token1 token2 vector 1 1 2 1 2 3 Where token1 is leaf and the number is the index in leaves table And vector numbers are indexes in a table that lists all syntax constructs So for x 1 the tables will be id token 1 x 2 7 id syntax 1 NameExpr UP 2 AssignExpr DOWN 3 IntegerLiteralExpr

Did you have a chance to look at the video https www youtube com watch v EJ8okcxL2Iw Yes I came here after watching it

The main idea is to assign a random vector to every kind of symbol whether that symbol is a path or a token Then during training these vectors are modified such that the loss term that we define is minimized That s basically how neural network are trained in a nutshell

Aha That makes it more clear thanks Now I need to find the place in code where the assignment of random vector takes place and see how these symbols are represented in Python Then the question would be what algorithm is used to adjust vector weights during training But that s probably already covered by paper

This is where the random vectors are initialized https github com tech srl code2vec blob master tensorflow model py L206 L220 The reader converts string inputs into integer indices and these integer indices allow looking up the specific random vector https github com tech srl code2vec blob master path context reader py L205 L207 The algorithm that is used to adjust vector weights during training is stochastic gradient descent backpropagation but that s a very common idea in training neural networks that is not unique to our work This idea is covered in almost any neural networks tutorial online course Best Uri

Writing down permalinks to avoid reference drift https github com tech srl code2vec blob e7547de9febe969cde7c64f20ebaa0ca5f4673b6 tensorflow model py L206 L220 Found the docs https www tensorflow org api docs python tf compat v1 get variable So for example path vocab is Tensorflow variable named PATHS VOCAB with shape 128 is probably the length of vocabulary in lines Vocabulary is loaded here https github com tech srl code2vec blob e7547de9febe969cde7c64f20ebaa0ca5f4673b6 vocabularies py L183 L184 and 128 is the width in floats for each path context The puzzling thing here is that it seems there is not 1 1 mapping between AST path components and floats And even if AST path is shorter it still gets 128 width vector So the network doesn t really have granularity at the AST level Paths are treated just as whole strings I am right https github com tech srl code2vec blob e7547de9febe969cde7c64f20ebaa0ca5f4673b6 path context reader py L205 L207 With gradient descent the goal is to find some minimum output value for a given set of inputs So here I guess the output value is the name of a function During training symbols and paths that are close to each other receive similar weighs which can serve as some coordinates in 3D or whatever D space and that allows to query the space for different properties This is my understanding of it so far

So the network doesn t really have granularity at the AST level Paths are treated just as whole strings Thus is correct and was addressed in a follow up paper Code2seq https code2seq org the goal is to find some minimum output value for a given set of inputs So here I guess the output value is the name of a function Yes but the minimum value that we re trying to find is the negative log probability of predicting the right method name During training symbols and paths that are close to each other receive similar weighs which can serve as some coordinates in 3D or whatever D space and that allows to query the space for different properties Thus sounds almost correct but I cannot completely confirm since I don t exactly understand what you mean by query the space for different properties

Hi yemao616 The topk metric basically means the fraction of test examples where the correct label is within the top k predictions This is meaningful in realistic settings imagine a code completion model that suggests some possible completions You don t necessarily need the correct prediction to appear first you only want the correct prediction to appear within the top 5 predictions or so So for example if the correct label original name was predicted 3rd then it would be considered as correct in top 3 top 4 top 5 In your case if there are only 4 possible classes and you would hypothetically used top 4 you ll get a top 4 accuracy of 100 as you can see in your top10 acc indeed the accuracy is 1 starting from the 4th entry I hope this helps Best Uri

Hi Makifer I think that the input for code2 seq can be used for code2 vec but not vice versa The reason is that in code2 seq the path is split to nodes e g ForStatement IfExpression VarDeclaration while in code2 vec the entire path is hashed into a single string of digits like 1234567 Additionally the statistics and histograms of the different models are computed slightly differently and also stored slightly differently So in general if you created a new custom dataset you can use it for both code2vec and code2seq but just follow the preprocessing scripts carefully to verify that the histograms and dictionaries are computed and stored the same

Hi urialon Thanks for explanation In our experiment we created a new C dataset using https github com JetBrains Research astminer library which generate paths astminer is referenced both in code2seq https github com tech srl code2seq extending to other languages and in code2vec https github com tech srl code2vec extending to other languages So we think that we can use the dataset with code2seq as well However astminer generates paths like this 12 885 72 where 12 is the first node id 885 is the path id and 72 is the last node id When we look at the https github com tech srl code2seq blob master README md java we noticed that in the preprocessed datasets paths include token names instead of token ids so we replace them in our generated dataset as well and we used those paths as input to code2vec To be clear our paths look like this int 885 fprintf where 885 is the path id Should we also put the entire path description to be able to use it with code2seq Or the current version should be fine

comments.body: Hi Simone Thank you for your interest in code2vec and for your kind words It s hard to tell One option would be to train the model using the boolean labels this will optimize your objective directly With some additional work you can also use your additional features and feed them into training If your dataset is too small it might be useful to train a model to predict method names on a larger dataset and then stop and fine tune the model using the binary classification labels The option you are suggesting of training for method names export the vectors and feed them into another binary classifier also sounds plausible It s difficult to tell in advance I suggest that you try all options it will be interesting to see a comparison of these approaches Best Uri P S our newer model code2seq https code2seq org performs better than code2vec even when the output is a label and not a sequence

It s hard to tell One option would be to train the model using the boolean labels this will optimize your objective directly With some additional work you can also use your additional features and feed them into training The idea of including the other features directly into the training phase seems interesting do you have any suggestion on how it could be done or where I should look in the code If your dataset is too small it might be useful to train a model to predict method names on a larger dataset and then stop and fine tune the model using the binary classification labels My dataset will contain around 15k methods they are extracted from students programming exercises so I will have many implementations of the same methods What do you mean by fine tune the model How could I do it The main problem here would probably be the training of the large dataset do you know by chance if someone has already trained a model for python on a large dataset P S our newer model code2seq https code2seq org performs better than code2vec even when the output is a label and not a sequence I was already considering to try it too since I believe that the preprocessing part is the same as the code2vec Sorry for the many questions and thank you for your help Simone

Including the other features requires to add them to the dataset file Please create a temporary dataset file and examine its structure every line is an example the first word is the target label that needs to be predicted and the rest of the 200 contexts are the paths that are the input of the network The next challenge would be to propagate them from the text file through the reader up to the model itself I think the easiest way will be to add these features space separated between the label and the path Then extend the csv record default currently it has 201 items you need it to have 201 number of features here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master path context reader py L82 Then hopefully you ll get the features as the elements 1 num features in row parts here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master path context reader py L185 And make sure that context str are taken from the correct indices here add num features to the beginning and end of the current indexing https github com tech srl code2vec blob master path context reader py L189 Then follow the code and see how the rest of the inputs such as the path contexts flow into the model Regarding training a Python model I don t know You might want to check previous closed issues because some people have asked about python in the past Best Uri

title: preprocessing problem about method names
body: Hi I am confused about preprocessing my own data and I need your help In preprocess sh it says that TRAIN DIR VAL DIR and TEST DIR should be paths to directories containing sub directories with java files each of TRAIN DIR VAL DIR and TEST DIR should have sub dirs and data will be extracted from java files found in those sub dirs So my own understanding is that the names of those sub dirs under TRAIN DIR VAL DIR and TEST DIR are the methods of the java files found in those sub dirs But after I preprocessed the data and trained the model then test the log showed something weird For example Original main predicted 1st main But there is no method name main in my data Can you help me figure it out

comments.body: Hi rrrxderek The names of those sub dirs under TRAIN DIR VAL DIR and TEST DIR are just names of repositories that the Java files came from and have no significance Regarding the name main I suggest that you check again if there s main or Main and verify that in the preprocess sh script you pointed to the right directories Best Uri
Hi Uri Thank you for the reply So what should I do if I want to add java files with new functions and new method names for training Should I just name the java files with their method name Best Derek

Just put them in the appropriate subdirectories Neither the names of the files nor the names of the directories don t matter You can also have files that have multiple methods in them You can download a raw un preprocessed dataset and take a look at its structure such as Java small or Java med See https github com tech srl code2seq blob master README md java Best Uri
Problem solved thank you

title: The file encoding of "dataset.train.c2v"?

title: New entries to dataset.dict.csv
body: Hi I am currently trying to preprocess java large on a server with 2 x Intel Xeon E5 2660 v3 which in total has 20 cores and 40 threads and 378GB of RAM However it is taking very long as mentioned in https github com tech srl code2vec issues 3 Currently I ve been running it for 12 hours and I am still extracting paths for training set I have a few questions regarding this 1 Is there a way to update the resulting dataset name dict csv file with only one project The use case is the following When I want to add new project s to train test validation set then instead of preprocessing the whole dataset again I d like to append them to the dataset name dict csv 1 1 I presume dict csv file is important when training from scratch not so important when continuing training since there is no need for the old dict csv entries anyway 2 What is the purpose of the JavaExtractor extract py I am asking because calling many jar instances seems to take quite a while and JavaExtractor 0 0 1 SNAPSHOT jar creates threads internally for every file anyway if called with dir argument I d call it directly and make some enhancements inside to speed it up skipping extract py Is there stuff that I might miss by doing this The raw txt files seem to only contain output from jar and nothing else Hope my questions do make sense Thanks in advance Hendrig

comments.body: Hi Hendrig Yes unfortunately processing such large datasets takes some time You can decrease the timeout here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master JavaExtractor extract py L39 to 5 minutes per directory or so such that directories that are not completed in time are skipped and their subdirs are extracted recursively except the few problematic subdirs which will be skipped This will be your best solution I think Another option is to try java med small first As for your questions 1 Yes it is possible The dict c2v file is a pickle file of a few dictionaries It is created here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master preprocess py L16 So if you load an existing dict update its values and re write it with the new values it is supposed to be fine but not continue training with a model that has started training with the old dict c2v only to start training a new model 1 1 This is correct when loading a trained model the necessary dictionaries are loaded from the model s files not from the dataset s files This is done here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master vocabularies py L178 2 The purpose of extract py is to wrap JavaExtractor 0 0 1 SNAPSHOT jar by running it using multiple processes while each jar uses multiple threads This hacky structure worked faster on my machines because sometimes too large files take all the JVM memory and stuck the whole jar running process Additionally if a jar process is taking too much time it is killed from outside from the extract py script and then re ran recursively on its subdirs Skipping extract py is possible but I don t see how it will speed up anything If you wish to run only a single process at a time you can just set it here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master JavaExtractor extract py L68 replace 4 with 1 I hope it helps

Okay I see it makes more sense now If I want to add the additional data to initial dataset I ll update the pickle file so others can train it from scratch instead of providing 2 datasets which people could also theoretically train on sequentially However I do have one question 1 If I want to keep training the model I ll just create a new entirely separate dataset with no pickle editing and use the load flag to load the trained model the data flag to point to the new dataset to train on and the save flag to provide a new save path This case is different and I presume it is okay to keep training a model that started with the old dict c2v

Hi hsellik So if I understand correctly you wish to do transfer learning where you train on dataset A and then continue training or fine tune on dataset B This is definitely possible just keep in mind that if the first training set was not large diverse enough some tokens and paths in the second training set will be treated as unknown Alternatively if you add names and paths from the new dataset Dataset B into the existing dictionaries this may work as well The only problem is that old names will be already trained and mixed with new names that appeared first in the training set of dataset B which will start as randomly initialized vectors but I guess there s no other choice in this case I am guessing that code2seq https github com tech srl code2seq will perform much much better at this transfer task because code2vec is much more sparse But that s a cool idea I would love to hear how it went

Hi urialon Yes I want to keep training further train the model Although I don t know if it can be classified as transfer learning since the problem remains the same In summary I have trained a binary classification model on a dataset Dataset A and want to further train on a new dataset Dataset B with the same problem and no new labels but avoid tokens and paths being treated as unknown I want to do that because I have a fair amount of computing power for Open Source Software projects but very limited computing capability at the location of the target project The classification problem remains the same Basically the question is do the Further training instructions in README https github com tech srl code2vec downloading a trained model 35 gb which can be further trained suffer the same unknown token problem as described in our discussion

Hi hsellik OK I see Basically the question is do the Further training instructions in README suffer the same unknown token problem as described in our discussion Yes It does suffer BUT I think that if Dataset A is large enough you ll find that most 90 of the tokens and paths in Dataset B are already in the vocabulary Maybe the easiest first step will be checking that hypothesis by simply counting comparing histograms before training You can check both 1 How many of the unique paths tokens from Dataset B are already in the vocabulary created by preprocessing Dataset A 2 How many of the occurrences of paths tokens from Dataset B are already in the vocabulary created by preprocessing Dataset A I guess that this one will be much higher than the former Then you can try both 1 Continue training on Dataset B without any change to the vocabularies 2 Continue training on Dataset B but add Dataset B specific common tokens paths into the dictionaries and into the embedding matrices will require a minor tensorflow work of taking the already trained embedding matrix and extending it with fresh uninitialized rows edit I meant randomly initialized rows I am also guessing that if you work with code2seq instead you won t need any vocabulary extensions or modifications and you will be able to just continue training on Dataset B since code2seq works with nodes instead of full paths you won t have unknown nodes in Dataset B since code2seq works with subtokens instead of tokens the probability of observing an unknown sub token is very small Good luck let me know how it goes
That s perfect thank you for the very thorough answers I ll let you know how it goes Will definitely use code2seq as well and compare the results

title: code vector vs target embedding
body: Hi Uri I m confused about code vecor and target embedding In Readme Exporting the trained target method name embeddings python3 code2vec py load models java14 model saved model iter8 save t2v models java14 model targets txt Exporting the code vectors for the given code examples The flag export code vectors allows to export the code vectors for the given examples 1 To my understanding code vectors are generated after combined context vectors and attention weights target embeddings are weights between code vector layer and softmax layer So they are different Each method name can be represented by code vector or target embedding if the method name is in the target tag dictionary Is my understanding right 2 When exporting the code vectors for the given code examples the output file doesn t contain method names Is it possible to add method named in the output file 3 When using the gensim python package in your example you use target embeddings Can we use code vectors as well Thanks

comments.body: Hi DavidSUN2 1 The code vectors and the target embeddings are trained to be close to each other but they are different as you say this is right The vector of a specific method name e g sort is shared among all the methods that are labeled as sort whereas the code vector of each of these examples is slightly different than the others 2 Yes it is possible to add method names although sometimes you need the code vector of a new given method and you don t have any given method name I don t have the capacity to do it myself right now but it is not supposed to be difficult at all If you re trying to do that and have any questions feel free to ask 3 Definitely yes as long as you have a given label method name or just ID number for each code vector I hope it helps Feel free to ask any more questions Best Uri

Hi urialon Thanks for your reply The code vectors and the target embeddings are trained to be close to each other I m confused about this Why are they close to each other by training Could you please do more explanation Thanks In addition target embeddings are weights between code vector layer and softmax layer Is this right

Hi DavidSUN2 Sorry it is indeed not trivial First yes target embeddings are weights vectors between the code vector and the softmax layer Second during training the softmax cross entropy loss encourages the code vector to have a large value of dot product with the correct target embedding the target embedding of the true label and a low dot product with each of the rest of the target embeddings So eventually it makes the code vector its corresponding true target embedding be close to each other in the euclidean space This is a characteristic of softmax cross entropy which is not specific to code2vec
Thanks a lot urialon I understand

Exactly In general the encoder of code2seq is better because it learns paths and names using LSTMs node by node while in code2vec the paths are monolithic For additional differences between code2vec and code2seq see Section 6 in the code2seq paper https openreview net pdf id H1gKYo09tX

Hi DavidSUN2 I don t think you need to change the loss Binary classification is a special case of multi class classification As long as the model sees only two possible labels during training this is binary classification If you change the loss to tf nn sigmoid cross entropy with logits you can allow the model to assign multi labels i e the same example can be both true and false Regarding the extractor it depends on where do you get your true false labels from This is the line that prints the method name as the label https github com tech srl code2vec blob master JavaExtractor JPredict src main java JavaExtractor FeaturesEntities ProgramFeatures java L21 https github com tech srl code2vec blob master JavaExtractor JPredict src main java JavaExtractor FeaturesEntities ProgramFeatures java L21 So instead of stringBuilder append name you can stringBuilder append anything else I hope it helps

Is it possible to load a TF model with the TF keras implementation 1 We haven t yet published any trained Keras model We may do so in the future 2 The published code does not currently support loading the trained TF weights using the Keras implementation 3 However it is technically possible to write a script that does it To do so one might have to change the names of the weights as you suggested I would i check the names of the variables both in the Keras TF implementations then ii create a mapping TFImplVariableName KerasImplVariableName and finally iii write a script that loads a weights file of the TF model and outputs a new one after applying the mentioned mapping 4 Notice also that except the variable names the Keras implementation uses different saving mechanism than the TF implementation This means that you also might have to make additional adaptations like having the checkpoints file I would train the Keras model for one epoch on a tiny dataset just to let it save a checkpoint to understand its structure If it requires merging PAD and UNK this is fine Indeed But the default configuration set it that way so no need to change anything More information about it There is a configuration parameter named SEPARATE OOV AND PAD https github com tech srl code2vec blob c98e8f786b7262e56c93e520d039fb7aa5d0f7ef config py L70 that should be set to False this is actually the default value Moreover I believe that all the default parameters values matches the configuration used to train the published trained TF model

Hi urialon I am also trying to use code2vec for binary classification RIght now I am playing around with a super small dataset but I observed that I get results like True 34 False 33 Since they do not add up to 100 I started debugging and noticed that there is a PAD OR OOV in raw prediction results which takes rest of the percentage Am I supposed to select the best from these values or is there a way to avoid the OOV value having an effect on my labels I have edited the JavaExtractor to output either True False as label and also changed MAX TARGET VOCAB SIZE to 2 Thanks in advance Hendrig

Hi hsellik First you probably should better use code2seq even for binary classification 1 One option is to select the argmax among true false ignoring the PAD OR OOV 2 Second I think that if you train on a large enough dataset for a long enough time you will see that the PAD OR OOV probability will be almost zero because the model won t see any OOVs in the training set 3 If you wish to completely mask the option to assign any probability to PAD OR OOV you can mask it before the softmax Here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master tensorflow model py L225 take the logits tensor these are the scores for every possible class before applying softmax and add minus infinity to the index that represents PAD OR OOV which is supposed to be index zero This should be something like logits logits tf log 1 tf one hot indices 0 depth tf shape logits 1 Explanation tf one hot will create a vector like 1 0 0 0 0 Then 1 tf one hot is 0 1 1 1 1 Finally applying the tf log will make this vector be inf 0 0 0 0 Adding this to the original logits will keep all values the same except for the first column that corresponds to the PAD OR OOV symbol This will not allow the model to assign any probability to PAD OR OOV at training time At test time do the same for the scores tensor here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master tensorflow model py L296 Let me know if this works

comments.body: Hi James You are right This is indeed a bug Thanks for letting me know However I think that the effect of this bug is very minor If I fixed it now it will break the already trained models because the paths at test time will not be exactly as they were at training time So if you are going to train a new model you can definitely fix it in your version and train a model on the fixed paths If you take one of our trained models just keep it as is the effect is very minor

Yes sure The idea is to help the model to distinguish between children of the same parent where the order is important For example the children of a Call node i e myObj foo are the object and the called method name if a path from myObj goes to some other node in the AST we want to let the model know that myObj is the first child of Call rather than the second child So the path will look like myObj Name0 Call target And the path coming from foo to target will look like foo Name1 Call target This way hopefully the model will be more expressive So the idea was to add this child id to nodes whom the order matters for their parent nodes such as myArray index myObj foo foo myArg Does it make sense

Ok so childID s are included when the child s type isn t enough to distinguish it from it s siblings For example AssignExpr has two Expression childen target and value which can both be leaves so target and value are distinguished by their childIDs If that s the purpose why are the childID s of the source and target elements in a path always included even if their type is unique among its siblings

Exactly but not in all cases As a heuristic I added manually only for 4 5 cases and I think that I didn t include AssignExpr There no special reason You can try to add more types or add child id for all but I don t think it will matter that much At some point in the research we figured out that the source and the target nodes are the most important so as another heuristic I added child Id for them always But now I think that it doesn t matter that much as well

title: JavaExtractor: Incorrect path length calculation
body: In FeatureExtractor the length of a path is calculated as int pathLength sourceStack size targetStack size 2 commonPrefix line 140 I believe this is calculation is one more than the actual path length as it is counting the commonNode twice I suggest calculating the length as currentSourceAncestorIndex currentTargetAncestorIndex 1

comments.body: Hi James First thanks But it is actually counting edges and not nodes I e the length of the path is defined there as the number of edges Of course the length could have been defined as the number of nodes which is edges 1 but at the time I thought that counting edges makes more sense Additionally the commonNode is decreased from the path length twice so the result is the number of nodes in the path excluding the common node which equals to the number of edges I know it s a little confusing I just ran it in debug mode and verified Your suggestion makes the length even smaller by 1 I agree that maybe it could have made more sense to define the length as the number of nodes in the first place
Thanks for clearing that up So the smallest path length is 2 as paths will always have at least three nodes source parent target
Yes exactly

title: what is `mask` doing?
body: Hi urialon I have a question about the code of building model What is mask doing https github com tech srl code2vec blob master model py L309 L311 I can predict that this code is related to updating parameters of attention weight but I could not read how it corresponds to the formula of the paper Thank you

comments.body: Hi Every example has up to max contexts contexts tuples of paths and their tokens which is set to 200 by default https github com tech srl code2vec blob master common py L18 However most methods have less than 200 contexts So we pad these examples with dummy contexts such that all examples will have the same shape and we can batch all examples together So the model computes attention scores for each of these 200 contexts But not all of them are real some of them are just paddings So before computing the softmax we add the value minus infinity to the scores that were computed for these padded contexts such that after softmax ing their attention weights would be zero and these paddings will not get any attention softmax squashes minus infinity to zero Let me know if you have any more questions Best Uri
I got it Thank you very much

comments.body: Hi Max Yes There is a simple way to extract the code vectors of a given example First If you want to get the code vector of a single example at a time use the predict command line flag that allows interactive prediction Alternatively if you want to convert a large batch of files to vectors preprocess those files using the preprocess sh scripts point the test dir path to your files the training and validation paths don t matter Then use your new test c2v file with our trained model and our dictionary bin and use the test command line flag In the function build test graph https github com tech srl code2vec blob master model py L329 the variable code vectors holds the batch of code vectors You just need the function to return this variable as an additional return value In the function that calls build test graph which is predict https github com tech srl code2vec blob master model py L356 if you re in predict mode and evaluate https github com tech srl code2vec blob master model py L134 if you re in test mode receive the additional return value E g in evaluate Instead of self eval top words op self eval top values op self eval original names op self build test graph self eval queue get filtered batches Replace the first line with self eval top words op self eval top values op self eval original names op self code vectors op Then whenever you re calling self sess run with these return values as arguments if you re in test mode it s here https github com tech srl code2vec blob master model py L159 add the new self code vectors op to the list of variables to run and add a receiving variable Instead of top words top scores original names self sess run self eval top words op self eval top values op self eval original names op feed dict self eval placeholder batch Use top words top scores original names code vectors self sess run self eval top words op self eval top values op self eval original names op self code vectors op feed dict self eval placeholder batch the difference is that self code vectors op is passed to the self sess run method and that code vectors is received And that s it the variable code vectors is now a numpy matrix where each row title: Unsuccessful TensorSliceReader constructor: Failed to find any matching files for models/java14m/saved_model_iter8
body: Hi I tried to run code2vec model and faced with problem associated with mistake in README I used trained model from https s3 amazonaws com code2vec model java14m model tar gz When I run python3 code2vec py load models java14m saved model iter8 predict I saw this Unsuccessful TensorSliceReader constructor Failed to find any matching files for models java14m saved model iter8 The reason is that archive contains model with name saved model iter8 release If we run like below all will be fine python3 code2vec py load models java14m saved model iter8 release predict Please fix README or rename model in archive Thanks
